record.name: Test and assemble a small material-bound canopy
record.function: Assess and construct a finite five-pole shade canopy from measured short materials, with actual grass trials, proof loads, exposure readings and maintenance.
record.costs: Exact IDs or one item:/object: prefix. Inspect/assess/exposure: one round/0.2 energy. Trial: one measured whole pole, one unaltered grass allocation >=0.1 unit, separate real weights; two stages/0.5 each. Assembly: first pole is ridge, next four legs, individually measured; positive explicit dimensions, 0.05 leg joint allowance, actual grass cover mass >=0.5 per roof area and six bindings >=0.02 mass each with personally passed source coupons; four stages/0.75 each. No splicing. Proof requires real load allocations; order names ridge midpoint, first end apex, second end apex, with conservative reaction envelope. Proof/dismantle: two stages/0.5 each. Repair replaces whole equal-quantity grass components in two stages/0.5 each, followed by two actual proof-load stages/0.5 each. Resume/cancel use only own project with empty target/components; unused dimensions zero. Trials use actual x/y layout and zero dimensions. Structure service uses target and zero dimensions. No energy/access means no progress or charge.
record.effects: Paid real geometry and conserved location-bound components; no supplied stock or automatic certification. Five poles form two triangular ends and a ridge; measured lengths bound all dimensions. Grass binding law 50 force per dry mass, wet factor 1–0.5, slip above half breaking force; actual apertures, wear 0.001 dry to 0.004 saturated per round. Explicit proof checks self/wet/wind/load weight, joints, bending, buckling, spread and sag. Conditional finite rays and actual body coverage reuse existing bounded thermal/rest effects and personal-refuge events. No assembly/mastery reward; informative paid trials/exposure use shared deduplicated understanding. Cancel/death releases only surviving unincorporated escrow once; installed parts and passive weathering persist.

execution.progress: Exact location-bound stages and paid effort; paused work resumes only remaining stages, completion cannot restart.

projects.question: Can measured short branches and local dry grass support a useful small canopy?
evidence: Tick 185: the cover trial completed both paid stages with an actual pole, grass coupon and stone weight.
The final trial recorded force 1.962, slip 0.045, aperture 0.15, sag 0.0109, no breakage and passed=false.
The trial components remain at (16.3,16), and the grass coupon is altered rather than pristine construction stock.
projects.uncertainty: The trial did not pass; the specific acceptance limits and whether a feasible revised allocation exists need review. Binding joints and the complete frame remain untested.
projects.goal: Establish material feasibility before committing construction supplies.
outputs: A retained altered grass coupon and bounded cover-response finding.
projects.missing: A passing covering configuration, tested bindings and sufficient individually measured poles.
projects.next: Review the full canopy capability contract before allocating further materials.
projects.benefit: Established a bounded covering response without injury or committing a full structure.

projects.question: Can available, physically tested materials support a useful resting refuge?
evidence: Tick 149: item-142-moss-834 measured usable length bounds of 0.75–0.85 world-coordinate units.

projects.goal: Establish material feasibility before committing construction materials.
completedSteps: Measured and load-tested the earlier specimen.

projects.question: Can I obtain suitable materials for a calibrated food mass assay?

projects.goal: Establish usable material evidence without treating relative resistance as absolute certification.
completedSteps: Completed two directional scratch contacts and inspection of both surfaces.
